item.title: Brad Mooar appointed new Fijian Drua head coach
item.description: The Fijian Drua have appointed highly regarded New Zealand coach Brad Mooar as Head Coach of the Swire Shipping Fijian Drua Men ahead of the 2027 Shop N Save Super Rugby Pacific season. Mooar, who has signed a two-year contract, will officially join the club in September 2026 to oversee preparations for the new campaign.
item.content:encoded:
The Fijian Drua have appointed highly regarded New Zealand coach Brad Mooar as Head Coach of the Swire Shipping Fijian Drua Men ahead of the 2027 Shop N Save Super Rugby Pacific season.

Mooar, who has signed a two-year contract, will officially join the club in September 2026 to oversee preparations for the new campaign.

He arrives with an impressive coaching résumé, having helped guide the Crusaders to three consecutive Super Rugby titles, served as an assistant coach with the All Blacks and Scotland, and previously led Welsh club Scarlets.

His appointment follows what the Drua described as an extensive international recruitment process involving Fijian Drua and Fiji Rugby leadership, along with an independent expert.

Fijian Drua Chief Executive Officer Jeff Miller said Mooar emerged as the standout candidate from a highly competitive field.

“This is one of the most important appointments in the short history of the Fijian Drua and we were determined to conduct a genuinely exhaustive process.”

Miller said the club received applications from an outstanding group of coaches but Mooar distinguished himself through his technical expertise, player development credentials and leadership qualities.

“Brad stood out through his technical and tactical knowledge, his experience in championship-winning environments, his understanding of player development and, importantly, his ability to build strong relationships.”

He added that Mooar understands the responsibility that comes with coaching Fiji’s Super Rugby franchise.

“Our purpose is to win Super Rugby Pacific, inspire a nation and change lives for the better. He has embraced that responsibility and we firmly believe Brad is the right person to lead the next phase of our journey.”

Mooar said he was honoured to take on one of the Southern Hemisphere’s most unique coaching roles.

“It’s a tremendous honour to be given the opportunity to lead the Drua and coach Fiji’s team in Super Rugby Pacific.”

He said the opportunity to work with Fijian players and culture was a major attraction.

“What drew me to this role is the chance to work with such wonderful athletes, to be part of a culture and a people I deeply admire, and to help build something meaningful for the nation.”

Mooar said his goal is to build a team capable of playing an exciting brand of rugby while competing for championships.

“We want to inspire the country, win championships and continue to grow our people and the game in Fiji by creating something the country can be truly proud of.”

He also congratulated the McDonald’s Fiji Drua Women, who recently secured the 2026 Super Rugby Women’s minor premiership and earned the right to host the Grand Final.

Mooar is currently an assistant coach with the Crusaders, having returned to the franchise in 2025 after previously helping the club win Super Rugby titles in 2017, 2018 and 2019.

His coaching career has also included roles with the Scarlets, the All Blacks, Scotland, the Southern Kings, Eastern Province Kings, and Southland. A former Mid Canterbury first five-eighth, Mooar is also a qualified lawyer.

The Drua said further announcements regarding the men’s coaching staff will be made in due course.

item.title: Star emerges
item.description: LELEAN Memorial School fullback Ratu Apenisa Nayalatabua Navikutu is open to considering an overseas rugby contract if the opportunity arises after his outstanding performance in the Eastern Zone Secondary Schools Under-18 Dean’s final. Navikutu made the comments after being asked whether he would consider moving overseas if the Fijian Drua did not offer him a contract.
item.content:encoded:
LELEAN Memorial School fullback Ratu Apenisa Nayalatabua Navikutu is open to considering an overseas rugby contract if the opportunity arises after his outstanding performance in the Eastern Zone Secondary Schools Under-18 Dean’s final.

Navikutu made the comments after being asked whether he would consider moving overseas if the Fijian Drua did not offer him a contract.

The man-of-the-match was instrumental in LMS’s 29-17 victory over Ratu Kadavulevu School on Saturday, producing a near-perfect performance with the boot – converting eight penalties – while directing play from the back.

“If an opportunity comes, whether it’s in Fiji or overseas, I’ll sit down with my family and carefully consider all the options before making a decision on what’s best for my future,” he said.

Navikutu admitted he did not expect to finish the final with eight successful penalty goals.

“I honestly didn’t expect to kick that many penalties. During the game I just shut out all the noise, focused on each kick and made sure I got the ball over,” he said.

His accurate kicking proved decisive, stretching LMS’s lead to 18-5 at halftime with another penalty on the stroke of the break.

However, the talented fullback’s influence extended beyond his goal-kicking.

He orchestrated LMS’s attacking structure, organised the defensive line and produced three try-saving tackles to deny RKS during its second-half fightback.

His all-round display has prompted calls from rugby followers for the Fijian Drua to monitor the emerging playmaker closely before overseas clubs secure his services.

Navikutu’s rise has been rapid. He joined LMS this year after transferring from Nakasi High School.

Before arriving at LMS, he played senior division club rugby for Lokia village in Rewa, an experience he credited with preparing him for this year’s schools campaign.

“I’m grateful to Lelean Memorial School for believing in me and giving me the opportunity to showcase my rugby,” he said.

Originally from Navolau, Rakiraki, Ra, with maternal links to Lokia in Rewa, Navikutu has emerged as one of the standout performers of this year’s Eastern Zone competition.

Following his man-of-the-match display, his rugby future appears brighter than ever.

item.title: Babasiga Lions edge Navua
item.description: THE Babasiga Lions left it until the closing stages to secure a hard-fought 1-0 victory over Navua in a tightly contested Extra Premier League clash. After a goalless first half, Navua frustrated Labasa with a disciplined defensive display, denying several scoring opportunities.
item.content:encoded:
THE Babasiga Lions left it until the closing stages to secure a hard-fought 1-0 victory over Navua in a tightly contested Extra Premier League clash.

After a goalless first half, Navua frustrated Labasa with a disciplined defensive display, denying several scoring opportunities.

The breakthrough finally came with only a few minutes remaining when Melvin Mani found the back of the net after being set up by teammate sparking celebrations amongst the players.

Labasa coach Alvin Chand praised his players for sticking to the game plan despite the strong challenge from a powerful Navua side.

“I’d like to thank my players. They played really well. We knew Navua would give us a tough run and that’s exactly what happened,” Chand said.

“The boys maintained their discipline and carried out our match plan properly. Credit also goes to Dan for providing the assist for Melvin’s goal.”

Chand said he reminded his players during the halftime break not to force opportunities in attack and to remain patient.

“I told the boys to use their options well and not rush play in the attacking third. The goals would come if we used the right methods. The substitutes also made a big impact and changed the game.”

The win strengthens Labasa’s position in the league standings, with Chand describing next week’s clash against Ba as another crucial fixture.

“Every game matter because the competition is so tight. We’ll assess injuries, focus on recovery and then prepare well for Ba,” he said.

Chand also acknowledged the support of the club’s sponsors, officials and volunteers before thanking the large crowd for backing the team throughout the match.

The team will now shift its focus to their next outing against Ba this weekend.

In other matches Tailevu Naitasiri 3-2 Suva FC, Rewa 1-1 Nadi, Ba FC 4-1 Lautoka FC, Nadroga FC 1-0 Nasinu FC.

item.title: Binnu retains title
item.description: JUNIOR Binnu Singh needed less than one round to prove why he remains the WBA Oceania Super Bantamweight champion, stopping India’s Harjot Singh in the opening round of the Kings Boxing Promotions Bad Blood Show at the Vodafone Arena in Suva on Saturday night. item.content:encoded:
JUNIOR Binnu Singh needed less than one round to prove why he remains the WBA Oceania Super Bantamweight champion, stopping India’s Harjot Singh in the opening round of the Kings Boxing Promotions Bad Blood Show at the Vodafone Arena in Suva on Saturday night.

Originally scheduled as the main supporting contest, Binnu’s title defence was elevated to the headline bout after Mika Ravalaca’s opponent withdrew from the promotion.

The Valley Road-based champion wasted little time asserting his dominance, overwhelming Harjot with a flurry of punches before the referee stepped in to end the contest in the first round.

“It was important for me to make a statement,” Binnu said after the fight. “I trained hard for this title defence and I’m happy to retain my belt in front of the home crowd. I’m ready for whatever challenge comes next.”

The main supporting bout also ended inside the distance as Ravalaca stopped late replacement Jone Tabuarua in the second round. Despite taking the fight at short notice, Tabuarua showed plenty of determination before Ravalaca’s relentless pressure forced the stoppage.

“I respect Jone for accepting the fight at the last minute,” Ravalaca said. “I was prepared for a tough contest regardless of who stood in front of me, and I’m pleased with the performance.”

Fiji heavyweight champion Semi Dauloloma was pushed the distance by the durable Senivalati Ratu in one of the night’s most competitive contests. After six hard-fought rounds, Dauloloma earned a unanimous points decision to maintain his unbeaten run.

The result was quickly followed by a challenge from fellow heavyweight Joseph Kwadjo, who impressed with a fourth-round stoppage victory over Kimo Vakalalabure.

Kwadjo dominated the contest before forcing the referee to halt the fight in the fourth round. Afterwards, he made his intentions clear.

“I’ve got a lot of respect for Semi, but I believe it’s time we settled who is the best heavyweight around,” Kwadjo said. “The fans deserve that fight, and I’m ready whenever he is.”

Dauloloma welcomed the challenge, saying he would never shy away from facing the division’s top contenders.

“If that’s the fight the fans want, then let’s make it happen,” he said. “I’m always ready to defend my reputation in the ring.”

Elsewhere on the card, Isikeli Senidoko stopped Filise Nabua in another entertaining contest, while Lidia Qarasaumaka produced a composed display to defeat India’s Anam Khan by points.

One of the night’s biggest talking points came from Nauru’s Rock Anson, who enjoyed a dream professional debut by stopping Masitogi Rokotuva in their super welterweight contest.

The impressive performance announced Anson as another promising talent to watch in the Pacific boxing scene.

Kings Boxing Promotions delivered an action-packed evening, with five of the seven bouts ending inside the distance and an enthusiastic crowd treated to a series of explosive performances.

The promotion also set the stage for several intriguing future match-ups, with a potential heavyweight showdown between Dauloloma and Kwadjo now looming as one of Fiji boxing’s most anticipated contests.

item.title: SVC Raluve eyes redemption at national quarters
item.description: THE Saint Vincent College under-16 Raluve team will use the lessons and experience from their 7-19 loss to Adi Cakobau School in the Eastern Zone Secondary Schools under-16 Raluve final at HFC Bank Stadium in Suva last Saturday as motivation for redemption during this week’s national Raluve quarter-finals. Despite the defeat, the team heads into the national play-offs with plenty of confidence and
item.content:encoded:
THE Saint Vincent College under-16 Raluve team will use the lessons and experience from their 7-19 loss to Adi Cakobau School in the Eastern Zone Secondary Schools under-16 Raluve final at HFC Bank Stadium in Suva last Saturday as motivation for redemption during this week’s national Raluve quarter-finals.

Despite the defeat, the team heads into the national play-offs with plenty of confidence and determination to improve on their performance from the Eastern Zone final.

SVC struggled to contain a clinical ACS side in the opening spell and trailed at half-time without troubling the scoreboard.

However, the team responded with greater purpose after the break, scoring their only try and applying sustained pressure, but ACS held firm to seal the title.

For team manager Salote Nainoka, the result did little to overshadow what has been a remarkable journey for a squad made up largely of girls experiencing rugby for the first time.

“I’m really proud of the girls, their achievement, and how far we have come as a team to reach the final,” Nainoka said.

She added that the team’s progress was even more significant given rugby’s traditional status as a male-dominated sport.

“It’s a male-dominated sport, and I’m proud of what the girls have achieved. They have really grown in the game and have given their best to come this far,” she said.

With the Eastern Zone campaign now complete, SVC has turned its focus to the national quarter-finals, where the side hopes to build on its encouraging performances.

Nainoka has called on supporters to continue backing the team as the girls chase national honours.

item.title: McCutcheon breaks national record twice
item.description: FIJI swimmer Anahira McCutcheon delivered one of team Fiji’s standout performances at the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow, breaking the Fiji open women’s 50-metre butterfly record twice in the space of a day. McCutcheon first set a new national mark of 27.09 seconds in the heats to qualify for the semi-finals.
item.content:encoded:
FIJI swimmer Anahira McCutcheon delivered one of team Fiji’s standout performances at the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow, breaking the Fiji open women’s 50-metre butterfly record twice in the space of a day.

McCutcheon first set a new national mark of 27.09 seconds in the heats to qualify for the semi-finals.

She then went a few milliseconds quicker in the semi-finals clocking a time of 27.01 seconds to lower her record and complete a memorable day in the pool.

The double record-breaking effort was a major milestone for the young swimmer and one of Fiji’s highlights at the games.

In the men’s event, Samuel Yalimaiwai and Don younger competed in the 100m breaststroke, recording times of 1 minute 5.60 seconds and 1: 08.18 respectively.

Fiji’s men’s 4x100m freestyle relay team of Reuben Taylor, Don Younger, Hansel McCaig and Tolu Baledrokadroka also impressed, finishing in 3:33.08.

Taylor produced an outstanding opening leg, posting a personal best of 53.38 seconds to give Fiji a strong start.

The performances continue team Fiji’s impressive campaign in the pool, with national records and personal bests highlighting the progress of the country’s swimmers.

item.title: Wheelbarrow race raises record $250k
item.description: THE Frank Hilton Amazing Wheelbarrow Race has raised a record $250,000 to support children with disabilities across Fiji, marking the most successful fundraising campaign in the event’s 10-year history. The amount eclipsed last year’s total of $166,000, reflecting the growing support from businesses, sponsors and the wider community for the fundraiser, which continues to change the lives of childr
item.content:encoded:
THE Frank Hilton Amazing Wheelbarrow Race has raised a record $250,000 to support children with disabilities across Fiji, marking the most successful fundraising campaign in the event’s 10-year history.

The amount eclipsed last year’s total of $166,000, reflecting the growing support from businesses, sponsors and the wider community for the fundraiser, which continues to change the lives of children and their families through the services provided by Frank Hilton Organisation (FHO).

A total of 25 teams lined up for this year’s race, with Fortech emerging as the overall champion after a spirited day of competition.

However, organisers said the event has always been about much more than crossing the finish line first.

Celebrating a decade since the race was first introduced, organisers highlighted the impact the fundraiser has had over the past 10 years, describing the milestone as a celebration of lives transformed through the generosity of participants and supporters.

“This represents lives supported, services delivered and futures changed,” organisers said during the prize-giving ceremony.

They acknowledged that every team, sponsor and individual who participated had contributed to improving the lives of children with disabilities by helping them access vital support services provided by FHO.

“In your wheelbarrow you have carried hope, dignity and opportunity for the children and families we serve,” organisers told participants.

The event has evolved into one of FHO’s flagship fundraising activities, bringing together corporate organisations and community groups in a unique competition while raising awareness about the needs of children living with disabilities across Fiji.

Although Fortech claimed top honours in the race itself, Harcourts was recognised as the highest fundraising team after collecting the largest amount in donations, with Begel Boys finishing second in the fundraising category.

A total of six awards were presented during the prize-giving ceremony to recognise achievements in both racing and fundraising.

Organisers thanked all 25 participating teams, sponsors, volunteers and supporters for helping make the 10th anniversary event the most successful in the history of the Wheelbarrow Race.

They said the record fundraising total would enable FHO to continue delivering essential services and support programmes to children with disabilities and their families across Fiji, ensuring more children have access to opportunities that improve their quality of life and future.

item.title: Setareki leads Grammar back to Southern Zone glory
item.description: Suva Grammar School under-19 captain Setareki Radrodrolagi’s belief never wavered, even after his side suffered its only defeat of the Southern Zone Secondary Schools Rugby competition to Nasinu Secondary School in round six. That confidence was rewarded yesterday as Radrodrolagi led Grammar to a thrilling 25-19 victory over Nasinu in the U19 final, completing a remarkable turnaround and reclaimin
item.content:encoded:
Suva Grammar School under-19 captain Setareki Radrodrolagi’s belief never wavered, even after his side suffered its only defeat of the Southern Zone Secondary Schools Rugby competition to Nasinu Secondary School in round six.

That confidence was rewarded yesterday as Radrodrolagi led Grammar to a thrilling 25-19 victory over Nasinu in the U19 final, completing a remarkable turnaround and reclaiming the Southern Zone title.

The right deadlocks, who hails from Navucini in Naitasiri and has maternal links to Nakasaleka, Lagalevu in Kadavu, said the round-six loss became the motivation the team needed heading into the knockout stages.

“We lost to Nasinu in round six, but I told the boys to regroup because we would meet them again in the final,” Radrodrolagi said.

“We just had to reset, stay focused and believe in ourselves.”

His prediction came true as Grammar produced a determined performance to deny Nasinu the title in one of the most anticipated finals of the day.

Radrodrolagi said the team’s focus now shifts to the Vodafone Deans competition, where they hope to continue their winning momentum.

“We’re not going there just to participate. We’re going there to compete,” he said.

The captain admitted the victory was especially meaningful because Suva Grammar had not enjoyed the same level of dominance in the U19 grade over the past few years.

“This means a lot to us. Grammar has always had a proud rugby tradition and we’re happy to bring the Southern Zone title back to the school,” he said.

He also praised his teammates for their resilience throughout the campaign, saying every player contributed to the team’s success after bouncing back from the disappointment of their earlier defeat.

Radrodrolagi dedicated the championship to former teammate Paolo Bonolangi, who is currently in France, and to his coach for their guidance, encouragement and unwavering belief in the squad throughout the season.

The remaining finals also produced exciting contests across the grades. The U14 final between Suva Grammar 20-10 againts Marist Brothers High School, while Grammar claimed the U15 title with a 24-17 win over Mahatma Gandhi Memorial School.

MGM defeated Nasinu Secondary School 19-12 to win the U16 boys’ title, and Grammar edged Gospel High School 23-22 in the U17 final. In the Weet-Bix Raluve competition, Nasinu defeated Suva Grammar 15-12, while Lomary Secondary School defeated Mahatma Gandhi Memorial High School 18-0 to secure the U18 title.
